bullets: Built full-stack production anomaly detection system combining LSTM (sequence anomaly), Autoencoders (reconstruction error), and Isolation Forest (statistical outliers) in an ensemble pipeline
Integrated RAG pipeline using ChromaDB vector search + Azure OpenAI + Cohere embeddings to generate context-aware, natural language anomaly reports — not just alerts
End-to-end data pipeline: MQTT → FastAPI → PostgreSQL → ML inference → ChromaDB RAG → explainable report → React dashboard (real-time visualisation)
Full model lifecycle: training (TensorFlow/PyTorch), experiment tracking, model versioning, Docker microservices deployment, post-deployment performance monitoring
Achieved 60% faster incident detection and 25% throughput improvement in production

projects.title: Minimum Viable Guardrail (MVG) — AI Safety Research
projects.company: BTH · Supervisor: Dr. Sadi Alawadi · Collaborator: Prof. Tony Gorschek
projects.role: Sole researcher — introduced original constructs, ran all empirical studies
projects.problem: No lightweight, quantitative framework existed to measure or constrain the verification bottleneck in AI-integrated software systems — especially critical for regulated industries.
bullets: Introduced the V-Ratio (T_verify / T_generate) — original quantitative metric measuring verification-to-generation time ratio in AI workflows; empirical study across 372 PRs, 11 repos, 37 months yielded median V-Ratio of 166.4×
Demonstrated deterministic testing structural limitations via adversarial mutation: 717 mutations across 239 MBPP functions, 5 random seeds — Dead Failure Rate of 34.45% (std 0.00% across all seeds)
Built and evaluated Z-SAAP logic-based guardrail across 6 pipeline versions on a 956-case corpus; v6 achieved 49.91% Safety Score, 22.03% FPR, 62.03% accuracy, 1,258ms latency

Proposed Minimum Viable Guardrail (MVG): lightweight runtime safety envelope constraining probabilistic AI outputs within deterministic logical boundaries — applicable to any organisation scaling AI in production
Introduced original constructs: Verification Singularity, Verification Chasm, Epistemic Debt — with direct applicability to EU AI Act Articles 14/26 compliance
projects.impact: Original research applicable to responsible AI governance in banks, government agencies, and healthcare — directly maps to EU AI Act compliance
